reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a flash-loan arbitrage bot and directs viewers to connect a wallet, fund or send liquidity to a newly deployed contract, and pay gas. It claims that greater liquidity produces greater profit and that the remaining profit will return to the viewer's wallet within seconds or minutes. The frames show the wallet connection, contract deployment interface, and ETH transfer sequence, but do not establish that the code works, that the displayed balance resulted from the interaction, or that any profit was received.

citations.quote: Today I'm going to show you how to commence a flash loan on UniSwap.
You need to deposit at least 0.1 for the contract to execute correctly and complete the flash loan uniswap bot.
The higher the liquidity, the higher the profit.
any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.
Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.

opening.argument: Judge, the description supplies material risk context rather than presenting effortless certainty: it expressly says that flash-loan exploits have been used against vulnerable DeFi protocols and obtained very large sums. The narration also explains that gas is necessary, that insufficient gas can exhaust the contract, and that unused excess gas remains. Those qualifications make the presentation compatible with a risky technical procedure whose outcome requires independent verification, not a deceptive guarantee of success. The available record does not itself establish that any profit was actually received.

citations.quote: While they've proved popular, flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and get millions of dollars.
you can't over fund your contract It'll only use the amount of gas that It needs to run and you'll always have that money still left in your contract.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited funding and wallet steps establish what the procedure requires, but they do not establish deceptive intent or a guaranteed outcome. The description itself places the steps in a broader explanation of flash-loan technology and its risks, while the narration warns about gas exhaustion. The balance sequence also does not prove that the displayed amount was profit received from this interaction.

citations.quote: Flash loans are a type of uncollateralized lending that have become very popular in decentralized finance (DeFi).
the contract would exhausted because it wouldn't had any gas to run it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A general warning about exploits does not neutralize the concrete money-making pitch. The same description says the viewer must deposit funds, that more liquidity produces more profit, and that profit will return to the wallet within minutes. Gas cautions explain how to complete the transaction; they do not warn that the advertised return may be illusory.

citations.quote: The higher the liquidity, the higher the profit.
any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.
send the liquidity to the new contract code.

opening.argument: The primary subject is a technical, operational demonstration. The title identifies DApp development and a beginner no-code Solidity bot, and the narration says it will show how to commence a flash loan on UniSwap. The supplied frames depict Remix IDE, Solidity compilation, contract deployment, and wallet interaction, which is the ordinary sequence of a programming walkthrough. Showing how a smart-contract workflow is configured does not by itself certify the code, promise a result, or prove that viewers were solicited deceptively.

citations.quote: DApp Development | Beginner No Code Solidity Flash Loan Arbitrage Bot
Today I'm going to show you how to commence a flash loan on UniSwap.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the walkthrough contains instructions is consistent with its stated development purpose. The visible material is a Remix coding and deployment interface, not an independent testimonial or proof of earnings. The quoted instructions therefore show a demonstration of tool use; they do not establish that the code works, that a viewer must rely on the creator, or that the presentation is deceptive.

citations.quote: DApp Development | Beginner No Code Solidity Flash Loan Arbitrage Bot

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it development does not change what the tutorial tells viewers to do with money. It directs users to send liquidity to a newly deployed contract, pay gas, and execute a flash-loan attack, while claiming remaining profit will return to their wallet. The IDE setting establishes a technical workflow, not educational neutrality or a merely theoretical demonstration.

citations.quote: Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.
confirm the gas fees to execute the flash loan attack.
any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.

opening.argument: The records are also consistent with an ordinary software and blockchain-service workflow: a viewer uses a wallet, a browser IDE, a contract, and network gas to perform the described operation. The instructions do not ask for a password, seed phrase, or account credentials, and they do not describe recruitment, a downline, or payments to earlier participants. They describe transaction inputs and contract execution, while the supplied material does not independently establish that any balance change was profit or that the code delivered the promised result.

citations.quote: To get started, you need to have MetaMask browser extension installed.
connect to your metamask wallet so that you can interact with the contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: Funding a contract and paying network fees can be ordinary operational requirements for blockchain software; those facts alone do not identify a fraudulent mechanism. The supplied workflow contains no cited credential request, recruitment structure, or instruction to pay another participant. The displayed wallet activity is also not proof that the amount shown was a return from the procedure.

citations.quote: Before we can run the contract we have to fund it. We have to put gas money in the contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely a routine software purchase: viewers are told to transfer liquidity into a newly created contract and are told that greater liquidity means greater profit. The absence of passwords or recruitment does not address the central risk, because the claimed mechanism is a funded contract promising an automated return, and the records do not verify that return.
